preconditions.description: The first line of input is a single integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 10^4), representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == 2 and all(1 <= int(x) <= 2*10**5 for x in line.split()) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() and ' ' in line and not line.startswith('\n'))
preconditions.description: For each test case, the first line contains two integers n and m (2 ≤ n ≤ 2·10^5, 1 ≤ m ≤ 2·10^5), representing the number of vertices and edges in the graph.

preconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == 2 and all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in line.split()) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() and ' ' in line and 's' in line and 't' in line)
preconditions.description: For each test case, the second line contains two integers s and t (1 ≤ s, t ≤ n, s ≠ t), representing the start and end vertices of the path.

preconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == 2 and all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in line.split()) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() and ' ' in line and not line.startswith('\n') and not ('s' in line and 't' in line))
preconditions.description: For each test case, the following m lines each contain two integers u_i and v_i (1 ≤ u_i, v_i ≤ n), representing an edge between vertices u_i and v_i. The graph is undirected, connected, and has no loops or multiple edges.

preconditions.expression: all(len(line.strip()) == 0 or line.strip() == '\n' for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() == '')
preconditions.description: Each test case is preceded by a blank line.

postconditions.expression: all(len(stdout.split()) == t and all(0 <= int(x) <= 10**9 + 6 for x in stdout.split()), stdout.strip() != '')
postconditions.description: For each test case, output a single integer representing the number of paths from s to t whose length differs from the shortest path length by no more than 1, modulo 10^9 + 7.

postconditions.expression: all(int(stdout.split()[i]) == (sum(1 for path in all_paths if shortest_path_length - 1 <= len(path) <= shortest_path_length + 1) % (10**9 + 7)) for i in range(t))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is the count of all paths from s to t where the path length is within [shortest_path_length - 1, shortest_path_length + 1], modulo 10^9 + 7. Here, shortest_path_length is the length of the shortest path from s to t, and all_paths includes all possible paths (including those with repeated vertices or edges).
